[C01] Port of Tessalune, Q3 throughput. The Tessalune Free Harbor Authority recorded 4,812 container movements in the third quarter of fiscal 2291, a 6.3% drop against Q2. The authority blamed the grounding of the barge Ombrelle Dray near Pier Nine, which closed two of the six berths for most of the period. Harbormaster Ilsabet Corvane-Ruiz said the backlog of waiting vessels would clear by the eleventh of Marenth, provided no further weather delays occurred. Shipping agents reported that several carriers diverted cargo to neighbouring ports during the closure, and the authority expects to lose roughly a fifth of its seasonal contracts. A recovery plan will be presented to the board at its next meeting.

[C02] Cargo manifest 77-Delta. The freighter Marigold Sundry unloaded 212 tonnes of saltglass resin bound for Wexmoor Quay under customs code TQ-90-117. Inspectors checked the seals, weights and declared values against the shipping documents and found no irregularities. A second consignment, 40 crates of pearlwood shingles destined for a roofing contractor, was held at the gate for a missing seal and released two days later after the supplier sent a corrected certificate. The manifest also lists eight pallets of brass fittings, two sealed drums of marine varnish and a single unmarked box addressed to the harbor chaplain, which customs opened in the chaplain's presence and found to contain hymn books.

[C03] Pier Nine crane failure. Gantry crane Hollis-4 lost hydraulic pressure during a lift on the ninth of Marenth, leaving a loaded container suspended for nearly six minutes before the operator could lower it safely. Nobody was hurt. Engineer Padraig O'Brannigan-Seo traced the fault to worn seals supplied by Dunmarrow Fluidics and noted that the same batch had been fitted to two other cranes. Replacement seals arrived by night rail, and the crane returned to service after nineteen hours. The authority has ordered inspection of every crane fitted with the affected batch and has asked the supplier to cover the cost of the delay to cargo handling.

[C04] Tide and signal notes. Spring tides at Tessalune peak at 3.9 metres, and pilots must not enter the inner channel within forty minutes of high water because the current across the sandbar can exceed six knots. The lantern code for a vessel awaiting a pilot is two amber lights over one white. Fog horns sound three short blasts every ninety seconds whenever visibility drops below half a nautical mile. Vessels leaving the inner channel at night must show a green light at the masthead and keep a listening watch on channel twelve. The harbor office posts the tide tables each Monday and revises them whenever the barometer falls sharply.

[C05] Harbor dues schedule. Vessels under 400 gross tons pay 31 marks per day. Refrigerated holds add a surcharge of 9 marks per day, and hazardous cargo adds a flat 120 marks. Dues are waived for lifeboats and for the survey vessel Pale Heron, which the authority uses to chart the channel after storms. Vessels staying longer than fourteen days receive a ten percent discount on the daily rate, but the discount does not apply to surcharges. Late payment incurs interest of two percent per week, and the harbormaster may refuse a departure permit until all dues are settled. Disputes must be filed in writing within thirty days of the invoice date.
